section.content: 本发明的目的在于确保锂离子电池的电池性能和安全性。使用由分离功能层3a和支承层3b构成的间隔件3，并形成使分离功能层3a比支承层3b的孔隙直径小且孔隙率低的致密的构成，由此能够抑制金属异物从正极极板1侧向负极极板2侧移动，由此负极极板2侧处的金属异物的析出被抑制，因而能够确保电池性能和安全性。

The purpose of the present invention is to ensure battery performance and safety of a lithium ion battery. By using the separator 3 composed of the separation functional layer 3a and the support layer 3b and forming a dense structure in which the separation functional layer 3a has a smaller pore diameter and a lower porosity than the support layer 3b, it is possible to suppress the movement of the metallic foreign matter from the positive electrode plate 1 side to the negative electrode plate 2 side, and thereby to suppress the deposition of the metallic foreign matter on the negative electrode plate 2 side, and it is possible to ensure battery performance and safety.

Lithium ion batteryTechnical Field

The present invention relates to a lithium ion battery including a separator between a positive electrode and a negative electrode.

Background

The lithium ion battery includes a positive electrode containing a lithium transition metal oxide as an active material, a negative electrode containing carbon as an active material, an electrolyte solution containing an organic solvent in which a lithium salt is dissolved, and a separator disposed between the positive electrode and the negative electrode.

In the electrode of the lithium ion battery, metal foreign matter such as iron, copper, zinc, tin, cobalt, nickel, chromium, and the like may be mixed. The mixed metal foreign matter may be mixed into the battery in a solid or ionic state. The lithium ion battery may have a reduced output voltage, generate heat, and cause a fire failure due to the mixed metal foreign matter. In particular, when a foreign metal is mixed in the vicinity of the positive electrode, the foreign metal is ionized by the internal electric field and is guided to the negative electrode side. The ions are precipitated on the negative electrode to form dendrites, and the dendrites grow to reach the positive electrode from the negative electrode, thereby short-circuiting the positive electrode and the negative electrode. Such a short Circuit causes a failure in ocv (open Circuit voltage) of output voltage reduction, and further causes a failure in heat generation or ignition.

In order to suppress such a defect caused by the metal foreign matter, a conventional lithium ion battery has been proposed in which a positive electrode and a negative electrode are closely attached to a coating separator. With such a structure, there is no gap between the electrode and the spacer, and the metal foreign matter mixed at the time of assembly does not contact the electrode, and dendrite caused by the metal foreign matter is less likely to be generated (see patent document 1).

Documents of the prior art

Patent document

Patent document 1: japanese patent laid-open publication No. 2013-127857

Disclosure of Invention

Problems to be solved by the invention

However, in the conventional lithium ion battery, although the metal foreign matter mixed in at the time of assembly can be made inert, the metal foreign matter mixed in the positive electrode in the initial step cannot be removed, and when the metal foreign matter is ionized in the positive electrode, the ionized metal foreign matter moves to the negative electrode, and dendrite is generated in the negative electrode. The dendrite is generated, and the anode and the cathode are short-circuited, so that the output voltage of the lithium ion battery is reduced, or the lithium ion battery is heated and ignited to reduce the performance and the safety of the battery.

The present invention solves the above problems, and aims to ensure battery performance and safety of a lithium ion battery.

Means for solving the problems

In order to achieve the above object, a lithium ion battery according to the present invention includes: the separator is configured from a support layer and a separation functional layer having a smaller pore diameter and a lower porosity than the support layer, and one of the support layer and the separation functional layer is disposed on the first surface side and the other is disposed on the second surface side.

Effects of the invention

According to this configuration, by using the spacer composed of the separation functional layer and the support layer and forming a dense configuration in which the separation functional layer is made smaller in pore diameter and lower in porosity than the support layer, it is possible to suppress the movement of the metallic foreign matter from the positive electrode side to the negative electrode side, thereby suppressing the precipitation of the metallic foreign matter at the negative electrode side, and thus it is possible to ensure battery performance and safety.

Detailed Description

Embodiments of the present invention will be described below with reference to the drawings.

In the following description, the same reference numerals are given to the components that perform the same functions, and the description thereof is appropriately omitted.

(embodiment mode 1)

Fig. 1 is a sectional view showing a structure of a cylindrical lithium ion battery as an embodiment of the present invention. The cylindrical lithium ion battery illustrated in fig. 1 includes positive electrode plates 1 and negative electrode plates 2, and the positive electrode plates 1 and the negative electrode plates 2 are alternately stacked. Between the positive electrode plate 1 and the negative electrode plate 2, a separator 3 is disposed to prevent the positive electrode plate 1 and the negative electrode plate 2 from physically contacting. The stacked positive electrode plate 1, negative electrode plate 2, and separator 3 are wound in a cylindrical shape, and are arranged in a case 6 having a positive electrode tab 4, a negative electrode tab 5, an electrolyte 7, and the like, thereby constituting a cylindrical lithium ion battery. The electrolyte solution 7 is composed of, for example, a solution in which a lithium salt is dissolved in an organic solvent, and contains lithium ions as an electrolyte.

Next, the structure of the spacer 3 will be described with reference to fig. 2.

Fig. 2 is a sectional view schematically illustrating the configuration of the main portions of the positive electrode plate, the negative electrode plate, and the separator in one embodiment of the present invention.

The separator 3 according to the present invention is formed by laminating a separation functional layer 3a having pores and a support layer 3 b. The separation functional layer 3a is a dense structure having a small pore diameter and a low porosity, and the support layer 3b is a rough structure having a larger pore diameter and a high porosity than the separation functional layer 3 a.

The pore diameter is a diameter of a cross section perpendicular to a longitudinal direction of a pore portion of the membrane, and the porosity is a proportion of a volume of the pore portion in a volume of the membrane. The larger the pore diameter and the higher the porosity, the higher the liquid permeability, but the mechanical strength was reduced. In addition, the smaller the pore diameter, the smaller the size of the metallic foreign matter that can be prevented. The rejection of the pore-based material is determined by the size of the pore diameter, the density of the pores, and the thickness of the layer. For example, when the ion of the metal foreign substance to be mixed is solvated and has a diameter of 0.8nm or more and 1.0nm or less, the average diameter of the pores of the separation functional layer 3a may be 0.3nm or more and 0.8nm or less, and the porosity may be more than 0% and 1% or less.

In this specification, the average diameter is expressed as pores having an average diameter of 0.3nm or more and 0.8nm or less, and the size is defined as the interval between bonding chains of molecules constituting the film. This is a size that is difficult to measure by a usual method for measuring pore diameters such as a mercury porosimeter, and can be measured by a method for measuring pores in a functional layer of a reverse osmosis membrane such as a positron annihilation method.

In the spacer 3, the exposed surface of the separation functional layer 3a is defined as a first surface, and the exposed surface of the support layer 3b is defined as a second surface. That is, the pore diameter and the porosity of the spacer 3 on the first surface side are smaller than those of the spacer 3 on the second surface side, respectively.

Here, the separation functional layer 3a in the present embodiment is a layer having a function of blocking the transmission of ions or molecules having a predetermined size or more and transmitting ions having a size smaller than the predetermined size.

The average film thickness of the separation functional layer 3a used in the present embodiment is not particularly limited, but is preferably 10nm or more and 100nm or less. If the thickness is less than 10nm, the film may be defective due to insufficient strength, and if the thickness is more than 100nm, the movement of the object to be permeated, which is necessary for the battery reaction, is inhibited, thereby causing a decrease in battery performance. The average film thickness of the separation functional layer 3a is preferably thinner than the average film thickness of the support layer 3 b.

The material of the separation functional layer 3a is not particularly limited, but is preferably any one selected from regenerated cellulose, cellulose ester, polyacrylonitrile, polytetrafluoroethylene, polyester polymer alloy, polyamide, polyimide, polysulfone, polyethersulfone, polyethylene, polypropylene, polyvinylidene fluoride, polyvinyl alcohol, ethylene-vinyl copolymer, and polyvinyl chloride. Particularly, aromatic polyamide and cellulose acetate are more preferable.

Here, the support layer 3b in the present embodiment is a porous layer that supports the separation functional layer 3 a. Examples of the inorganic filler include, but are not limited to, a nonwoven fabric, a porous film, and the like. The support layer 3b has a pore diameter larger than that of the separation functional layer 3a and a high porosity, and therefore ions that have passed through the separation functional layer 3a pass through the support layer 3 b.

The average thickness of the support layer 3b used in the present embodiment is not particularly limited, but is preferably 15 μm or more and 100 μm or less. If the thickness is less than 15 μm, the possibility of film cracking due to insufficient strength is high, and if the thickness is more than 100 μm, the ratio of the volume of the separator in the internal volume of the alkaline battery is high, and the ratio of the positive electrode active material to the negative electrode active material is low, resulting in a decrease in battery capacity.

The diameter of the pores formed in the support layer 3b is preferably 100nm or more and 1 μm or less. If the particle size is less than 100nm, the movement of the permeable object necessary for the battery reaction is hindered, and therefore, the battery performance is lowered, whereas if the particle size is more than 1 μm, the possibility that the insulation between the positive electrode and the negative electrode cannot be ensured increases. The porosity is preferably 50% or more and 80% or less. If the amount is less than 50%, the movement of the permeable object necessary for the battery reaction is hindered, and therefore, the battery performance is lowered, whereas if the amount is more than 80%, the film may be broken due to insufficient strength.

The material of the support layer 3b is not particularly limited, but is preferably any one selected from regenerated cellulose, cellulose ester, polysulfone, polyethersulfone, polyvinyl alcohol, ethylene-vinyl alcohol copolymer, vinylon, polyamide, polyimide, polyethylene, polypropylene, polyester, and polyvinylidene fluoride.

As a method of manufacturing the spacer 3 of the present embodiment, first, the support layer 3b is prepared, and then the separation function layer 3a is formed on the support layer 3 b. The support layer 3b can be produced by melting or dissolving the material of the support layer 3b in a predetermined solvent, and then using a dry stretching method, a wet extraction method, a foaming method, or the like. Next, a solution of the material of the separation functional layer 3a was applied to the support layer 3b by a die coating method and dried to obtain the spacer 3.

The structure of the positive electrode plate 1 and the negative electrode plate 2 will be described with reference to the cross-sectional structures of the positive electrode plate 1 and the negative electrode plate 2 shown in fig. 2. The positive electrode plate 1 has the following structure: a current collector for positive electrode 1b using aluminum foil or the like is sandwiched between 2 positive electrode active materials 1a containing lithium metal oxide and a binder, and laminated using a binder. The negative electrode plate 2 has the following structure: a current collector for negative electrode 2b using copper foil or the like is sandwiched between 2 negative electrode active materials 2a containing carbon and a binder, and laminated using a binder.

The positive electrode plate 1, the negative electrode plate 2, and the separator 3 having the above-described structure are stacked in this order as shown in fig. 1, and the positive electrode plate 1, the separator 3, the negative electrode plate 2, and the separator 3 are wound and inserted into the case 6 together with the positive electrode tab 4, the negative electrode tab 5, the electrolyte 7, and the like, and sealed to complete the lithium ion battery.

In the example shown in fig. 2, the positive electrode plate 1, the negative electrode plate 2, and the separator 3 are arranged in a direction in which the support layer 3b contacts the positive electrode active material 1a and the separation functional layer 3a contacts the negative electrode active material 2a during winding. However, the separator 3 may be disposed so that the supporting layer 3b contacts the negative electrode active material 2a and the separation functional layer 3a contacts the positive electrode active material 1 a.

As described above, by using the spacer 3 composed of the separation functional layer 3a and the support layer 3b and forming a dense structure in which the separation functional layer 3a has a smaller pore diameter and a lower porosity than the support layer 3b, the separation functional layer 3a has a function of suppressing permeation of polyvalent metal ions, and the support layer 3b can secure the mechanical strength of the entire spacer 3 without lowering the permeability of liquid.

Here, the separation functional layer 3a is a thin film as follows: the pore diameter and the porosity are such that lithium ions in the electrolyte solution 7 sufficiently permeate therethrough and that permeation of foreign metal ions is suppressed, and the film thickness is not more than a certain value so as not to decrease the permeability of the electrolyte solution 7 and lithium ions.

The support layer 3b has a film thickness of a certain value or more in order to ensure the mechanical strength of the separator 3, and has a pore diameter and a porosity of a certain value or more in order not to affect the permeability of the electrolyte 7 and lithium ions. Thus, even if metal foreign matter is mixed into the positive electrode plate 1 in the initial step, dendrite formation is prevented, and precipitation of metal foreign matter on the negative electrode plate 2 can be suppressed, so that battery performance and safety can be ensured.

Specific examples are described below in further detail.

Fig. 3 is a diagram illustrating a structure of a spacer in example 1, fig. 4 is a diagram illustrating a structure of a spacer in example 2, fig. 5 is a diagram illustrating a structure of a spacer in example 3, and fig. 6 is a diagram illustrating results of evaluation of charge-discharge cycle characteristics of lithium ion batteries in examples and comparative examples.

(example 1)

In embodiment 1, a lithium ion battery in which iron, copper, zinc, tin, cobalt, nickel, and chromium having a diameter of 20 μm or more and 30 μm or less were mixed as foreign metal particles into the positive electrode active material 1a in an amount of 100ppm based on the mass of the positive electrode active material 1a was produced as example 1. In this case, the spacer 3 is used in which the separation functional layer 3a is not disposed on the side wall 10 of the support layer 3 b.

That is, in the separator 3 of example 1, as shown in fig. 3, the separation functional layer 3a is in contact with the negative electrode plate 2 only on the first surface 8 of the separator 3 which becomes the front surface, and the support layer 3b is in contact with the positive electrode plate 1 only on the second surface 9 of the separator 3 which becomes the front surface. Therefore, the separation functional layer 3a is not formed at the position of the support layer 3b in contact with the side wall 10 facing the positive electrode tab 4 and the negative electrode tab 5.

(example 2)

In embodiment 1, a lithium ion battery was produced in which iron, copper, zinc, tin, cobalt, nickel, and chromium having a diameter of 20 μm or more and 30 μm or less were mixed as foreign metal substances into the positive electrode active material 1a in an amount of 100ppm based on the mass of the positive electrode active material 1a, and this was taken as example 2. At this time, as shown in fig. 4, a spacer in which the separation functional layer 3a is also disposed in contact with the side wall 10 of the support layer 3b is used as the spacer 3. That is, the separation functional layer 3a is formed at a position in contact with the side walls 10 of the negative electrode plate 2 and the support layer 3 b.

(example 3)

In embodiment 1, a lithium ion battery in which iron, copper, zinc, tin, cobalt, nickel, and chromium having a diameter of 20 μm or more and 30 μm or less as foreign metal particles in the positive electrode active material 1a were mixed in an amount of 100ppm based on the mass of the positive electrode active material 1a was produced as example 3. In this case, as the spacer 3, a spacer is used in which the separation functional layer 3a is also arranged on the side wall 10 of the support layer 3b, and the thickness of the central portion of the separation functional layer 3a is smaller than the thickness of both ends (positive electrode terminal side and negative electrode terminal side). That is, the film thickness T3a of the separation functional layer 3a is set to be thicker at the center between the positive electrode tab 4 (see fig. 1) and the negative electrode tab 5 (see fig. 1) than at the outer peripheral sides of the positive electrode tab 4 (see fig. 1) and the negative electrode tab 5 (see fig. 1). In order to avoid concentration of stress locally applied at this time, the film thickness is gradually changed. In example 3, the description has been given of the configuration in which the separation functional layer 3a is also disposed on the side wall 10 of the support layer 3b, but in the configuration in which the separation functional layer 3a is not disposed on the side wall 10 of the support layer 3b, the thickness of the separation functional layer 3a may be thinner at the center than at both ends.

Comparative example 1

In embodiment 1, a lithium ion battery was prepared using a conventional separator without a separation function layer, and mixing iron, copper, zinc, tin, cobalt, nickel, and chromium as foreign metal substances having a diameter of 20 μm or more and 30 μm or less in the positive electrode active material 1a to 100ppm based on the mass of the positive electrode active material 1a, respectively, as comparative example 1.

The lithium ion batteries of examples 1 to 3 and comparative example 1 produced under the above conditions were subjected to constant current/constant current charge/discharge tests (upper limit voltage 4.2V, lower limit voltage 3.0V) with a charge current of 1.8mA and a capacity of 5.4mAh in an atmosphere of 25 ℃. The results are shown in FIG. 6.

From the results of fig. 6, it is clear that examples 1 to 3 are superior to comparative example 1 in charge-discharge cycle characteristics. That is, the lithium ion batteries according to examples 1 to 3, which are constituted by the spacer having the separation functional layer 3a, have a smaller decrease in battery capacity even when charging and discharging are repeated, as compared with comparative example 1, which is constituted by the conventional spacer.

The battery performance in comparative example 1 was significantly reduced due to the effect of mixing iron, copper, zinc, tin, cobalt, nickel, and chromium as foreign metal particles having a diameter of 20 μm or more and 30 μm or less in the positive electrode active material 1a, respectively, by 100ppm with respect to the mass of the positive electrode active material 1 a. This is considered to be because the metal foreign matter ionized on the positive electrode side moves to the negative electrode side, the metal foreign matter precipitates on the surface of the negative electrode plate 2, and the precipitate grows toward the positive electrode plate 1, whereby the positive electrode plate 1 and the negative electrode plate 2 cause an internal short circuit.

On the other hand, in the lithium ion batteries according to examples 1 to 3 using the separator 3 including at least the separation functional layer 3a, the average value of the pore diameters of the separation functional layer is smaller than the polyvalent ions solvated in the electrolyte and larger than the lithium ions. The separation functional layer 3a has pores with a pore diameter of 0.6nm to 2nm and a porosity of 10% to 30%. The various ions in the electrolyte solution are in a solvated state by the adsorption solvent depending on the charge amount, and the size of the solvated ions tends to increase as the valence increases.

Therefore, iron, copper, zinc, tin, cobalt, nickel, chromium, and the like, which are ions having a valence of 2 or more, are larger in an ion solvated state than lithium ions, which are monovalent ions. Therefore, the lithium ions can be transmitted from the positive electrode side to the negative electrode side to suppress the movement of the metal foreign matter ions, and the output voltage of the lithium ion battery can be suppressed from decreasing, or the lithium ion battery can be heated or ignited to suppress the battery performance and safety from decreasing, and the battery performance and safety of the lithium ion battery can be ensured.

Next, the charge-discharge cycle characteristics in examples 1 to 3 will be described as if they were good in the order of example 1, example 2, and example 3.

In example 1, the separation functional layer 3a is disposed only between the support layer 3b and the negative electrode plate 2, and the separation functional layer 3a is not disposed on the side wall 10 of the support layer 3 b. When a large amount of metal impurities are contained in the positive electrode plate 1, the ionized metal impurities diffuse in the vicinity of the positive electrode plate 1 and reach the negative electrode plate 2 through the separation functional layer 3a, but the ionized metal impurities are considered to be precipitated in the negative electrode plate 2 by capillary effect and to penetrate through the space between the side wall 10 of the support layer 3b of the separator 3 and the positive electrode tab 4 and the negative electrode tab 5 and reach the negative electrode plate 2.

On the other hand, in example 2, since the separation functional layer 3a is also disposed on the side wall of the support layer 3b, it is considered that the metal impurities are prevented from permeating between the side wall 10 of the support layer 3b of the separator 3 and the positive electrode tab 4 and the negative electrode tab 5, and the ionized foreign metal substances generated in example 1 are hardly permeated. Therefore, the charge-discharge cycle characteristics of example 2 are considered to be better than those of example 1.

The separation functional layer 3a has a small pore diameter and a low porosity, and therefore has a dense membrane, and therefore is less likely to pass through the electrolyte solution than the support layer 3 b. Therefore, the film thickness of the separation functional layer 3a is set to a film thickness that does not obstruct the flow of the electrolytic solution and suppresses the transmission of the metal foreign matter ions. In example 2, as shown in fig. 4, since the film thickness T3a of the separation functional layer 3a is sufficiently thin, the film thickness T3av of the spacer 3 is substantially the same as the film thickness T3b of the support layer 3b with respect to the flow direction of the electrolyte of the separation functional layer 3a disposed on the side wall of the support layer 3b, and as described above, the permeation of foreign metal ions in the vicinity thereof is substantially prevented. On the other hand, if the film thickness T3ah in the direction perpendicular to the flow direction of the electrolyte solution of the separation functional layer 3a disposed on the side wall 10 of the support layer 3b is thick, the width of the support layer 3b in the direction perpendicular to the flow direction of the electrolyte solution becomes narrow, and the flow of the electrolyte solution is hindered accordingly. Accordingly, the film thickness T3ah of the separation functional layer 3a disposed on the side wall of the support layer 3b is preferably smaller than the film thickness T3a of the separation functional layer 3a disposed on the surface of the support layer 3 b.

Here, a change in the shape of an electrode accompanying charge and discharge in a general lithium ion battery will be described. When charging a lithium ion battery, the value varies depending on the type of the electrode plate, but the negative electrode plate 2 expands by about 10% and the positive electrode plate 1 expands by about 2%. On the other hand, during discharging, both the positive electrode plate 1 and the negative electrode plate 2 return to their original states. However, the electrolyte is in a squeezed-out state and cannot be immediately recovered. Such expansion of the electrode plates during charging causes the innermost central portion of the electrode plate group to receive a pressure of about half the amount of the contained electrolyte solution, and this stress and the nonuniformity of the electrolyte solution amount become factors that deteriorate the charge-discharge cycle characteristics.

However, the film thickness of the central portion of the separation functional layer 3a in example 3 is smaller than the film thickness of both ends (positive electrode tab side and negative electrode tab side). Therefore, as compared with example 2, the liquid permeation is less hindered by the layer having a lower porosity in the central portion than in the both end portions, and therefore the electrolytic solution in the central portion easily permeates, and the variation in the amount of electrolytic solution is suppressed. Therefore, the charge-discharge cycle characteristics of example 3 are considered to be better than those of example 2.

In embodiment 1, the positive electrode plate 1, the negative electrode plate 2, and the separator 3 are arranged in the direction in which the support layer 3b contacts the positive electrode active material 1a and the separation functional layer 3a contacts the negative electrode active material 2a during winding, and the effect of suppressing the movement of the metal foreign ions as in embodiments 1 to 3 can be obtained even when the positive electrode plate 1, the negative electrode plate 2, and the separator 3 are arranged in the direction in which the separation functional layer 3a contacts the positive electrode active material 1a and the support layer 3b contacts the negative electrode active material 2a during winding.

However, when the separation functional layer 3a contacts the positive electrode active material 1a in which the metal foreign matter is easily ionized, the metal foreign matter ions in a locally high concentration contact the separation functional layer 3a, and even if the rejection rate of the metal foreign matter ions of the separation functional layer 3a is high, the amount of the metal foreign matter ions penetrating the separation functional layer 3a increases. On the other hand, when the support layer 3b is in contact with the positive electrode active material 1a and the foreign metal ions permeate through the support layer 3b to reach the separation functional layer 3a, the foreign metal ions diffuse to have a low concentration when permeating through the support layer 3b, and therefore the amount of foreign metal ions becomes small. Therefore, since the amount of metal foreign matters deposited on the surface of the negative electrode plate 2 is small, good charge-discharge cycle characteristics and safety can be obtained.

Next, the results of evaluating the blocking rates of lithium and iron, copper, zinc, tin, cobalt, nickel, and chromium, which are foreign metal substances, with respect to the separator 3 used in example 3 are shown in table 1.

Here, the evaluation of the blocking rate is defined by the concentration C1 of the target substance on the supply liquid side and the concentration C2 of the target substance on the permeated liquid side across the spacer, using the blocking rate R of the separation target by the spacer as an index, and is obtained by (1-C2 ÷ C1) × 100. Here, as the supply liquid, a solution in which a certain amount of lithium trifluoromethanesulfonate, iron trifluoromethanesulfonate, copper trifluoromethanesulfonate, zinc trifluoromethanesulfonate, tin trifluoromethanesulfonate, cobalt trifluoromethanesulfonate, nickel trifluoromethanesulfonate, chromium trifluoromethanesulfonate was added to ethylene carbonate was used.

A solution permeated by applying a pressure of about 0.3MPa to the supply liquid side through a spacer was used as a permeated liquid. Then, the concentrations of lithium, iron, copper, zinc, tin, cobalt, nickel, and chromium contained in the feed liquid and the permeate liquid were measured, and the blocking ratio (%) of each substance was calculated by the above-mentioned numerical expression. Note that the blocking rates of the respective substances are RLi, RFe, RCu, RZn, RSn, RCo, RNi, and RCr.

As is clear from table 1, the barrier properties RFe, RCu, RZn, RSn, RCo, RNi, and RCr of iron, copper, zinc, tin, cobalt, nickel, and chromium were higher than the barrier property RLi of lithium in the separator 3 used in example 1. This is because lithium is a 1-valent ion, while iron, copper, zinc, tin, cobalt, nickel, and chromium are multivalent ions, and the sizes of the ions in solvation are greatly different. From the results, it is also understood that the separator 3 used in the lithium ion battery of the present embodiment has the following functions: by utilizing the difference in the ion size, lithium necessary for the battery reaction permeates the separator, and the movement of the metallic foreign matter to be separated is prevented by the separator 3.

Next, the separation function and the blocking rate of the spacer will be described.

When the pore diameter is smaller than that of the separator 3 used in examples 1 to 3, the porosity is small (less than 50%) and the blockage size is small, the blockage rate RLi of lithium and the blockage rates RFe, RCu, RZn, RSn, RCo, RNi, and RCr of iron, copper, zinc, tin, cobalt, nickel, and chromium as the metallic foreign substances are larger than the values in [ table 1 ]. That is, not only the metal foreign matter but also lithium movement necessary for the battery reaction is hindered between the positive and negative electrodes, and therefore, the metal foreign matter is not suitable as a separator for a lithium ion battery.

In addition, when the pore diameter is larger than that of the separators used in examples 1 to 3, the porosity is larger (more than 80%) and the stopping size is larger, the stopping rate RLi of lithium and the stopping rates RFe, RCu, RZn, RSn, RCo, RNi, and RCr of iron, copper, zinc, tin, cobalt, nickel, and chromium as the metallic foreign materials are smaller than the value of [ table 1 ]. That is, not only lithium but also a metal foreign substance permeates the separator, and thus the intended effect of the present invention cannot be obtained.

As described above, it is necessary to make the rejection rates RFe, RCu, RZn, RSn, RCo, RNi, and RCr of iron, copper, zinc, tin, cobalt, nickel, and chromium sufficiently higher than the rejection rate RLi of lithium.

Industrial applicability

The present invention is useful for a lithium ion battery or the like having a separator between a positive electrode and a negative electrode, which can ensure battery performance and safety.
